limitations: One detached job, two process owners, two fresh generations and at most two recovery snapshots. Zero represents a legacy NULL generation and resource3 represents a different job.

The job is already due. Shared-capacity admission, queue ordering across multiple jobs, tenant authorization before repository calls and worker dispatch are outside this slice. The claim action includes the repository organization filter.
Lease age partitions preserve live expiry, expired within the30-second takeover grace, and outside grace. Matching owners may renew any age until recovery commits.

Resource existence is fixed for each case. Current, missing and foreign resource fences are separate cases. Deletion during execution and complete lifecycle revision and stop-intent bookkeeping remain separate protocols.

Recovery here projects successful retry onto status, generation, quiescence and lease ownership. Attempts, interruption and requeue budgets, canary-specific payload fences, dependent writebacks and object storage contents are not abstracted as proved.

Claimed payload hydration happens after the claim transaction. Successful response and response failure have the same database projection. The PostgreSQL hook checks both persistence and recoverability.
Weak fairness of each pending recovery completion establishes bounded call completion. Overall job completion depends on dispatch and external work and is not claimed.
